proof: bench/exploits.js -> p6b submits both escaping shapes ('../secret-canary.txt' and the bare '..') through the same dashboard route and asserts the handler rejects both before any tar invocation and no tarball is produced.

residualNote: The first version of this fixture rejected only names containing path separators, and the bare '..' - which has no separator - defeated it by packing the parent tree into the archive. A round-3 run-1 adjudicator found that defect; the guard now does a resolved containment check instead. The tar-behaviour side of this case is host-dependent (measured with bsdtar 3.8.8).
